name: archery
description: Architecture docs as code in VS Code: an arc42 document with a model-based UML editor for all 13 UML 2 diagram types, PDF/HTML export, and tools for Claude Code and GitHub Copilot that show their edits live.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No architecture documentation in this workspace.
[Initialize architecture documentation](command:archery.init)

archery.export.browserPath.markdownDescription: Path to a Chromium-based browser (Edge, Chrome, Chromium, Brave) used to print the document to PDF. Empty: detect an installed one.

languageModelTools.modelDescription: Add an element (component, actor, external system, use case, node, class, port, ...) to the shared model. The id is derived from the name unless given and never changes later. Use parent for nesting (component in package/component, port on component, artifact or execution environment in node). With `diagram` it is also placed on that canvas diagram (at x/y if given), or added as the last lifeline of that sequence diagram.

languageModelTools.name: archery_write_sequence_diagram
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create (or with overwrite: true, replace) a sequence diagram for a runtime scenario (section 6).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create (or with overwrite: true, replace) a sequence diagram for a runtime scenario (section 6). Lifelines are model element ids (actors, components, external systems); elements used in messages are added as lifelines automatically. Steps: {msg: {from, to, label, kind: sync|async|reply|create|destroy|self|lost|found, async?: true for an asynchronous self/lost/found message, gate?: true when the missing end of a lost/found message is a gate on the frame (from / to outside the interaction)}}, {fragment: alt|opt|loop|par|break|critical|neg|strict|seq|ignore|consider|assert, branches: [{guard, steps}], min?, max? (loop iterations: loop(min,max), max "*" = unlimited)}, {fragment: "ref", label, over: [ids]}, {note, over: [ids]}. Embed with <!-- archery:diagram diagrams/<name>.seq.json -->.

name.description: File name without extension; default: kebab-case of the title

roles.description: Role names per lifeline id, shown as "role : Type" (default ":Type")

notation.description: Draw the interaction as a sequence diagram (default) or a communication diagram (participants with links and numbered messages)

languageModelTools.name: archery_write_timing_diagram
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create (or with overwrite: true, replace) a timing diagram: how the state of participants changes over time (section 6 runtime, or section 10 quality scenarios with deadlines).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create (or with overwrite: true, replace) a timing diagram: how the state of participants changes over time (section 6 runtime, or section 10 quality scenarios with deadlines). Lifelines: {ref: model element id, role?, form?: "state" (state timeline, default) | "value" (compact value lifeline), states: [top to bottom], changes: [{at, state}]}. Messages: {from, to, at, arrive?, label, kind: sync|async|reply}; leave out from (or to) for a message from (or to) a gate on the frame; from = to is a self message. Constraints: {on: lifeline id, from, to?, label}: a duration constraint from..to such as "0..2s", or a time constraint / observation at `from` (e.g. "t = now") when `to` is missing. Times are numbers in `unit` (e.g. "ms"). Embed with <!-- archery:diagram diagrams/<name>.timing.json -->.

name.description: File name without extension; default: kebab-case of the title

unit.description: Time unit shown on the axis, e.g. "ms"

end.description: End of the time axis (default: after the last event)

languageModelTools.name: archery_get_data
languageModelTools.userDescription: Items of a structured arc42 list stored in data/*.yaml.
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Items of a structured arc42 list stored in data/*.yaml. Lists:
- requirements (section 1.1, key field "id"): id, heading (chapter heading), title, text (Markdown), type (e.g. "Functional requirement"), status, priority, parent (id of the requirement or heading it is under; the list is in document order), specification, satisfiedBy (list of model element ids: the building blocks that satisfy it), goals (list of quality goal ids it refines), attributes (map name -> text: other attributes of a requirements tool), reqif (ReqIF identifier, set by import_reqif; keep it)
- quality-goals (section 1.2, key field "id"): id, priority (integer, 1 = highest), quality (e.g. ISO 25010 / Q42 characteristic), goal, motivation
- stakeholders (section 1.3, key field "role"): role, contact, expectations (towards the architecture documentation)
- constraints (section 2, key field "id"): id, category (technical | organizational | convention), constraint, explanation
- quality-overview (section 10.1, key field "category"): category, description
- quality-scenarios (section 10.2, key field "id"): id, name, kind (usage | change), quality, goals (list of quality goal ids), priority; short form: context, stimulus, metric; long form: source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, responseMeasure
- risks (section 11, key field "id"): id, kind (risk | debt), title, description, priority (high | medium | low), probability, impact, mitigation
- glossary (section 12, key field "term"): term, definition, translations (map language -> term), synonyms (list)

- quality-goals (section 1.2, key field "id"): id, priority (integer, 1 = highest), quality (e.g. ISO 25010 / Q42 characteristic), goal, motivation
- stakeholders (section 1.3, key field "role"): role, contact, expectations (towards the architecture documentation)
- constraints (section 2, key field "id"): id, category (technical | organizational | convention), constraint, explanation
- quality-overview (section 10.1, key field "category"): category, description
- quality-scenarios (section 10.2, key field "id"): id, name, kind (usage | change), quality, goals (list of quality goal ids), priority; short form: context, stimulus, metric; long form: source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, responseMeasure
- risks (section 11, key field "id"): id, kind (risk | debt), title, description, priority (high | medium | low), probability, impact, mitigation

languageModelTools.name: archery_add_local_node
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a node that exists only on this diagram: a note, or a state machine / activity node.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Add a node that exists only on this diagram: a note, or a state machine / activity node. Kinds: note, state, initial, final, choice, junction, fork, join, history, deepHistory, terminate, region, entryPoint, exitPoint, action, activityFinal, flowFinal, decision, merge, object, partition, sendSignal, acceptEvent, acceptTimeEvent, pin, interruptibleRegion, interactionUse, interaction. States take "text" for internal activities (one per line, e.g. "entry / start timer"); partitions (swimlanes), states, regions and interruptible regions contain other local nodes via parent; parent can also be an element shown on the diagram (a note inside a component). Orthogonal regions: "region" nodes with a state as parent (they fill the state, separated by dashed lines). entryPoint / exitPoint sit on the border of their parent state; a "pin" sits on the border of its parent action; acceptTimeEvent is the hourglass (name e.g. "every 5 min").

languageModelTools.name: archery_write_data_table
languageModelTools.userDescription: Replace all rows of a structured arc42 list (data/*.yaml) at once, and/or its column layout (visible columns, their order, labels and widths; extra columns become custom fields on the items).
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Replace all rows of a structured arc42 list (data/*.yaml) at once, and/or its column layout (visible columns, their order, labels and widths; extra columns become custom fields on the items). Omit rows to change only the layout: the rows stay exactly as they are. Rows are objects of field -> text; numbers, comma-separated lists and "key: value" maps are converted per field. Rows without an id get one. fit: "auto" makes the export fit the column widths to the content (columns with a width keep it); fit_table_columns fits them once. Lists:
- requirements (section 1.1, key field "id"): id, heading (chapter heading), title, text (Markdown), type (e.g. "Functional requirement"), status, priority, parent (id of the requirement or heading it is under; the list is in document order), specification, satisfiedBy (list of model element ids: the building blocks that satisfy it), goals (list of quality goal ids it refines), attributes (map name -> text: other attributes of a requirements tool), reqif (ReqIF identifier, set by import_reqif; keep it)
- quality-goals (section 1.2, key field "id"): id, priority (integer, 1 = highest), quality (e.g. ISO 25010 / Q42 characteristic), goal, motivation
- stakeholders (section 1.3, key field "role"): role, contact, expectations (towards the architecture documentation)
- constraints (section 2, key field "id"): id, category (technical | organizational | convention), constraint, explanation
- quality-overview (section 10.1, key field "category"): category, description
- quality-scenarios (section 10.2, key field "id"): id, name, kind (usage | change), quality, goals (list of quality goal ids), priority; short form: context, stimulus, metric; long form: source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, responseMeasure
- risks (section 11, key field "id"): id, kind (risk | debt), title, description, priority (high | medium | low), probability, impact, mitigation
- glossary (section 12, key field "term"): term, definition, translations (map language -> term), synonyms (list)

rows.description: All rows; omit to keep the current rows

width.description: Column width in percent of the table; omit for automatic

columns.description: Visible columns in order; omit to keep the current layout

merges.description: Merged cells (spreadsheet style); omit to keep the current ones

fit.description: "auto": the export fits the column widths to the content; null: widths as set; omit to keep

languageModelTools.name: archery_fit_table_columns
languageModelTools.userDescription: Balance the column widths of a data table (data/*.yaml): as few wrapped lines as possible and no word wider than its column.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Balance the column widths of a data table (data/*.yaml): as few wrapped lines as possible and no word wider than its column. The table is measured in a browser (Edge, Chrome or Chromium) with the export's own fonts and layout, on the exported page (screen) and on the printed page (print: page size, orientation and margins from the export settings). Starting from the current widths, width moves between columns while the table gets shorter. Returns the widths in percent before and after (in the order of `fields`), `lines` (the lines all body cells are drawn with; a cell is as tall as its row) and `tallestCell` per target as [before, after], and the cells whose own text still takes 3 or more lines. apply: true saves the widths in the table's view (only the column widths change); fitting again gives the same widths. columns: limits per field in percent { min (default 3), max, fixed (keeps its current width) }.

targets.description: screen: the exported page; print: the printed page (page size, orientation and margins from the export settings). Default both

apply.description: true: save the widths; false (default): only propose them

languageModelTools.name: archery_import_reqif
languageModelTools.userDescription: Import requirements from a ReqIF file (.reqif, or a .reqifz archive; the OMG Requirements Interchange Format of DOORS, Polarion, Jama, codebeamer, Capella, ReqIF Studio and others) into the requirements list (data/requirements.yaml, shown in chapter 1.1).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Import requirements from a ReqIF file (.reqif, or a .reqifz archive; the OMG Requirements Interchange Format of DOORS, Polarion, Jama, codebeamer, Capella, ReqIF Studio and others) into the requirements list (data/requirements.yaml, shown in chapter 1.1). Every requirement of the file's specifications becomes a row in document order: id (from ReqIF.ForeignID), heading (ReqIF.ChapterName), title (ReqIF.Name), text (ReqIF.Text, as Markdown), type, status, priority, parent (its place in the hierarchy), specification, and its other attributes. Importing again updates the requirements from the file and drops the ones the file no longer has; Archery's trace links (satisfiedBy, goals) and requirements added in Archery stay. The file is kept as data/requirements.reqif, so export_reqif writes it back with only Archery's changes. `file`: relative to the workspace, or absolute.

languageModelTools.modelDescription: Export the requirements (data/requirements.yaml) as a ReqIF file for a requirements tool, with the architecture they trace to: quality goals, quality scenarios, constraints, decisions and the building blocks that satisfy requirements, each as a specification of its own, and the trace links as relations (Satisfies: building block -> requirement; Refines: requirement or scenario -> quality goal; Addresses: decision -> requirement, quality goal or constraint).
